headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Replit Agent’s writable, networked Repl can ingest MinerU outputs and secrets, creating default-path exfiltration and corruption risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU can emit parsed document text via API/MCP, and Replit Agent can read/write Repl files and act on workspace content. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if MinerU output is copied into the Repl or a shared file. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF MinerU output is pasted into a Replit workspace file or prompt
IF Replit Agent treats extracted document text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep MinerU output in a separate, read-only folder
Prefix all imported text with a non-executable delimiter
Require manual review before Replit Agent acts on extracted text
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between MinerU and Replit Agent

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, OCR text, and can expose them through APIs/MCP; Replit Agent reads workspace files, handles secrets, and has broad network egress. If sensitive documents are moved into the Repl, Replit can transmit context or secrets outward, making leakage plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are imported into the Repl workspace
IF Replit Agent sends workspace context or secrets to external services
mitigations: Do not place sensitive documents in the Repl workspace
Store secrets only in a separate vault, not in files
Review outbound network destinations before running the agent
Redact sensitive fields before handoff from MinerU
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on agent outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU is multi-threaded and can use MCP/API surfaces, while Replit Agent has execute_shell, write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and persistent workspace state. Both can mutate shared files if connected to the same workspace, so concurrent writes and git corruption are a realistic default-path conflict.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same Repl workspace or mounted directory
IF MinerU output is written into files that Replit Agent also edits
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate directory
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches for all edits
Check in changes after each agent run
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted facts from documents, and Replit Agent can act on workspace content and deploy code. If Replit treats MinerU output as authoritative without verification, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect code or deployment actions. The pair is not inherently unsafe, but the handoff lacks a built-in verification step.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses MinerU-extracted text as ground truth
IF no human or automated verification step checks extracted facts before action
mitigations: Require a second-pass review of extracted facts
Compare key fields against the source document
Limit MinerU output to suggestions, not commands
Block deployment actions until verification passes
requires-engineering: add schema validation between extraction and action

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is documented as private/offline and processes document classes including OCR text, while Replit Agent handles secrets and runs in a cloud Repl with broad egress. If regulated or confidential documents are processed in Replit, residency and retention expectations can be violated. The mismatch is driven by Replit’s cloud handling; MinerU is not the compliance problem here.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are placed into the Replit workspace
IF the deployment lacks a DPA, residency controls, or retention limits
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Replit
Use anonymized samples for Replit runs
Confirm residency and retention settings before upload
Separate secret handling from document processing
requires-engineering: obtain contractual and technical compliance controls
